trust_decision.summary: Each scaffolder SCM action decides which credential authenticates its SCM call: the user-supplied input token, or a fallback to the backend's privileged integration credential (GitHub credentials provider/App, GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure integration token). The fix adds an opt-in scaffolder.requireScmUserCredentials flag that forbids the fallback. The decision is made per action and in the shared helpers getOctokitOptions (GitHub), getClient/getToken/createGitlabApi (GitLab) and fetchContents via UrlReader (fetch:*).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'unintended GitHub authentication fallback'. getOctokitOptions is the single GitHub helper that falls back from the caller's token to the integration credentials provider when no token is given.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about GitHub mutation/publish actions authenticating with the backend's credential. fetch:* actions are generic, read-only template fetchers in the core plugin that 'just read the template', so a solver can argue they are a neighbouring feature. Likewise, other SCM modules (GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure) can be argued out of a 'GitHub' report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: With the flag on, fetches from non-github/gitlab integrations (Bitbucket Server, plain HTTPS hosts, file:// relative template paths) must still work without a token, because only GitHub/GitLab UrlReaders accept a user token. With the flag off (the default), the integration-credential fallback must keep working everywhere. An over-broad fix that rejects every tokenless fetch, or that ignores the flag, breaks these.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: publish:bitbucketCloud resolves git push auth a second time with the same token-or-integration fallback, separately from the API header at :219-221
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix left this second fallback untouched (it is only shielded by the earlier throw). A maintainer could plausibly have placed the guard only around the API header, which would leave the git push falling back.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: defaultClientFactory calls getOctokitOptions without the flag; the PR action relies on its own pre-check before clientFactory
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Custom clientFactory and wrapper paths are common. Moving the guard into getOctokitOptions alone would miss the PR action, and a guard only in the action would miss direct getOctokitOptions users.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fetch:cookiecutter (and fetch:rails at plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-rails/src/actions/fetch/rails/index.ts:191) reads SCM content through fetchContents with the integration credential
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: They have no token input, so upstream documents them as unaffected. In our copy, adding a token input there would create a realistic, distant sibling of fetch:template.
